checks: Read s332 output (sections A, F) and the six Q53 report entries. Per-bin 1-0 numbers are internally consistent: HCN/HCO+ N 0.86-0.94, S 0.46-0.69 in every |v|<100 bin, so per-bin N/S 1.4-1.9 with no sign change. Agree the round-1 core50 inversion was a channel-selection artefact and the contrast is a line-core property, not a wing/outflow one.

Agree the decomposition bracket (rho 0 to 1 gives N/S 1.30-1.65) is the right way to handle model dependence; an HCO+ boost covering at most ~12% of the contrast is plausible and the 28 K km/s HCN-free HCO+ requirement is a good consequence calculation.
Agree N-rich wing and CN wings are correctly NOT claimed. Note the N 1-0 100-200 bins (HCN/HCO+ 1.11-1.34 at 4-5 sigma) are marginal and the 3-2 non-reproduction is sensible.

Spot check of section F: HCN R32/10 N 0.306, S 0.217 (S/N 0.71) vs HCO+ 0.404/0.359. This is a large (~30%) HCN excitation/opacity difference, and it contradicts the project's earlier 'HCN 3-2/1-0 equal at N and S' statement and the earlier report entries (e.g. Q16/Q38 ladders). The worker flagged but did not reconcile it. It is the most consequential number for the main question (excitation vs abundance) and is left unexploited.

I did not re-run the pipeline; checks rely on the printed output and on the worker's null-bin test, which is adequate for the core ratios (stat 1-3%) but the systematics (bin edges 1.36-1.83 on HCN core) are large relative to the quoted +-0.02.

fixes.what: Reconcile the matched-beam R32/10 with the earlier 'equal HCN 3-2/1-0' statement and earlier ladders, and revise or annotate the conflicting report entries.
fixes.why: The two statements cannot both stand; the reconciliation (aperture, beam, continuum/baseline, pbcor, HCN 1-0 hyperfine/contaminant, 3-2 line fully in band) determines whether HCN is subthermally excited at S.
fixes.how_experts_do_it: Measure R32/10 for HCN and HCO+ at both nuclei with the identical circular beam, same aperture, same velocity window, in Tb; vary beam 1.4-3.5 arcsec; list the earlier numbers' apertures side by side; state which is right and flag the superseded report entries.

fixes.what: Carry the excitation difference to a quantitative non-LTE bound on how much of the N/S HCN/HCO+ contrast (1.48 at 1-0, 1.85 at 3-2) excitation alone can produce.
fixes.why: The verdict says 'abundance not demonstrated' without testing it. The 1-0 vs 3-2 contrast difference plus the R32/10 values give two constraints that a pure abundance difference (same n, T) and a pure excitation difference predict differently.
fixes.how_experts_do_it: RADEX/LVG grid in n, Tkin, N/dv per species at both nuclei, fit HCN and HCO+ 1-0 and 3-2 (plus HNC) with beam-filling and Tbg, and report: (a) best-fit [HCN]/[HCO+] N and S with allowed ranges; (b) the contrast reproduced with equal abundance ratio. Even a bracket (e.g. thin, LTE vs sub-thermal) is better than none.

fixes.what: Tighten the core N/S systematic: quote the HCN/HCO+ N/S as a range with bin-edge/velocity-window dependence rather than 1.48+-0.01.
fixes.why: Edge choices give 1.36-1.83, so the +-0.01-0.02 statistical error is not the real uncertainty and overstates confidence ('high').
fixes.how_experts_do_it: Use moment-0 over the full line (zero-level FWHM windows set from HCO+ and applied identically), plus peak-pixel spectrum ratio, and quote one number with an honest systematic; lower confidence on entry 1 accordingly.

fixes.what: State HCO+ 1-0 self-absorption/opacity and 13CO(2-1) opacity caveats as a bound on the X/13CO result.
fixes.why: X/13CO N/S (2-3.5) is presented as a column proxy but 13CO(2-1) is moderately thick and was measured at higher resolution then convolved; it is only supportive.
fixes.how_experts_do_it: Use a 13CO/C18O ratio if available, or give the N/S result as a bracket for tau13 0-1; otherwise keep it as qualitative support and label confidence low.

notes_for_questioner: If the HCN R32/10 deficit at S (0.71 of N) is confirmed, HCN is sub-thermally excited or less dense at S than HCO+: is the HCN/HCO+ contrast then mainly a density/excitation signature of S gas (AGN heating/XDR/mechanical) rather than an N-species abundance change? Matched-beam H13CN/H13CO+ and HCN/HCO+ at 4-3 would break the degeneracy.
